solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pay heed to appropriate reminder

parts.note: to appropriate something is to take it for yourself
a note is a short written reminder

explanation.surface: An instruction to heed a suitable memo left for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective describing the reminder, but it is the verb meaning seize.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe paying attention to something and registering it in the mind.

clue.text: New Orleans and his biggest part

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over afresh into a different order

explanation.surface: New Orleans and one man claiming most of something, as if the city belonged to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of the city's name but is the anagram signal on ORLEANS and HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from Aesop's fable, where the lion takes the largest portion of the spoils.

clue.text: Excitable Oriel blue's not easily held in place

indicators.note: excitable letters are agitated and jump into a new order

explanation.surface: An Oxford sportsman from Oriel College, a 'blue', is too excitable to keep still.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is an Oxford college; a blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone defiant and unruly resists control, so is hard to keep in check.

clue.text: Jam servicemen in here?

definitions.meaning: a jam is a predicament or muddle
soldiers and sailors eat together in their dining hall

explanation.surface: Wondering whether military men are stuck in a traffic jam here.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddle or fix is one sense; an armed forces dining room is the other.

clue.text: Soft chump's amorous advance

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for soft
a chump is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A gentle fool makes a romantic move.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a pass at someone is to make a romantic or sexual approach.

clue.text: Pioneer one going for support

indicators.note: going means the word one departs from the letters of pioneer

explanation.surface: A trailblazer leaves and someone else steps in as backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one going for' reads as a substitution, but the word ONE simply leaves PIONEER; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar or pile holding up a bridge or arch is a structural support.

clue.text: Hero of Rome in rough sea, neat for the most part

indicators.note: a rough sea is churned up, so these letters are tossed about
only most of the word neat is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A Roman hero sailing a rough sea, mostly tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts NEAT to NEA, which joins SEA in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan prince of Virgil's epic, legendary ancestor of the Romans.

clue.text: Lampoon settled fury

parts.note: settled, as on a perch, means sat
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A cartoon mockery that calmed someone's rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a mocking piece of writing, a kind of ridicule.

clue.text: She tests chopper circling digger

indicators.note: circling here means turning round, so the word for chopper runs backwards

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
a miner digs underground

explanation.surface: A woman puts a chopper round a digger to test it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' suggests one piece going round another, but here it means turning about, so EXA is the chopper read backwards; 'She' is just an example of the tester.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who sets and marks a test; 'she' is just one example of such a person.

clue.text: Lair housing a cleric

indicators.note: housing means the lair contains the a

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A hideout sheltering a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior clergyman in charge of a cathedral chapter is a churchman.

clue.text: Life of Riley from undemanding cryptic setter

parts.note: something undemanding is easy

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured, so the letters of setter are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A comfortable life earned from an easy-going crossword compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a comfortable, carefree existence of ease and plenty.

clue.text: Manager is a stud too

definitions.meaning: the person in charge at work
a raised knob or ornament, as on a shield

explanation.surface: A manager who is also a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor is one sense; a decorative knob or protuberance is the other.

clue.text: Elaborate titles about essential touchstone

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the word for essential
elaborate means work up, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a must is something essential

explanation.surface: Fancy titles grouped around a fundamental benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' gives LITEST, which goes 'about' the word for essential; a litmus test is the chemist's acid check, now used figuratively.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a decisive criterion or benchmark by which something is judged.

clue.text: What sets Thucydides off? A letter with aspiration

definitions.meaning: the historian's name in Greek begins with this letter
a Greek letter pronounced as an aspirated T

explanation.surface: Asks what begins the Greek historian's name, then describes a breathy letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Thucydides' name in Greek starts with this letter; 'aspiration' also hints at ambition, but here means breath.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth Greek letter originally represented a breathed T sound.

clue.text: Randomly survey it in place of study

indicators.note: randomly means these letters are mixed up in no fixed order

explanation.surface: An instruction to conduct a random survey in a study area.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution of higher learning is a seat of study.

clue.text: Old printer is kind to me

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
the clue's writer refers to themself, the crossword setter

explanation.surface: The setter claims an old printer was good to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' looks like an adjective meaning generous but is a noun, sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor who set type by hand was a traditional printing worker.

clue.text: Cheapskate found holding back cheese

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read backwards
holding means the letters are held inside the words cheapskate found

explanation.surface: A miser caught hoarding some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Asterix's mate finally dropped Roman daggers

indicators.note: finally dropped means the last letter, the one for Roman, falls away

parts.note: Obelix is the companion of Asterix the Gaul in the comic books
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The cartoon Gaul's friend at last abandons Roman weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman daggers' reads as one phrase, but Roman is the numeral X to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are dagger-shaped marks used in printing for references or doubtful passages.

clue.text: Mere kitty

definitions.meaning: a mere is a small lake
a kitty is a shared fund of money

explanation.surface: Just a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small body of water is one sense; a common fund of money is the other.

clue.text: Duck, as it happens, goes with Polish dressing

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
a broadcast shown as it happens is live
to oil wood is to rub it to a shine

explanation.surface: Duck served with a Polish sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb, rubbing a surface with oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad dressing is commonly made from this pressed fruit fat.

clue.text: Place with no atmosphere is free, peer's upset about account

parts.note: someone let out is free

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for account
upset means the letters of peer's are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A dull venue where a nobleman is cross about a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges PEERS to ERSPE, which goes 'about' AC.
explanation.definitionFit: The vacuum beyond Earth has no air, so literally lacks any atmosphere.

clue.text: American fuel is blended to be profitable

indicators.note: fuel that is blended is mixed, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: US petrol is mixed to be more lucrative.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings benefit or advantage is profitable in the broad sense.

clue.text: Steal crop

explanation.surface: Pinch the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is one sense; a small cut with scissors is the other.

clue.text: Bumped into core of strong Irish police in capital

parts.note: to bump into someone is to meet them

indicators.note: the core is the central letters of the word strong

parts.note: polis is a dialect word for police in Ireland and Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone encounters tough Irish police in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A major city, especially the chief city of a country, is its capital.

clue.text: Station where taxis wait, turned off

definitions.meaning: a taxi ... is where cabs queue
food that has turned has gone off and smells foul

explanation.surface: A cab stand that has been switched off.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab stand is one sense; foul-smelling and spoiled is the other.

clue.text: Box crammed with large parcel

indicators.note: crammed with means the large letter is stuffed inside the box

parts.note: a pot is a container, a box of sorts
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A box stuffed with a big package.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel of land is a small plot.

clue.text: Fellow leaving instrument finds another

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for fellow departs from the instrument

parts.note: a flute is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A man walks out on his instrument and picks up a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: another instrument, following on from the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked string instrument is a second instrument after the first one named.

clue.text: In the Athenaeum in those days

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words the Athenaeum

explanation.surface: Life at the old London gentlemen's club in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The Athenaeum is a London gentlemen's club.
explanation.definitionFit: Both refer to a time in the past, at that period.

clue.text: Scab to spoil plaster

parts.note: milk that turns has spoilt
to plaster a surface is to coat it

explanation.surface: Messing up the plaster over a wound's scab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scab' looks medical but means a strikebreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker betrays fellow workers, as a traitor switches sides.

clue.text: Position article next to little sibling

parts.note: the is the definite article
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: An item placed beside a small brother or sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition put forward for argument is a stated stance.
